title: Learning Analytics: Engagement, Assessment, and Outcome Forecasting
question: Can weekly course records identify an upcoming assessment problem early enough for a person to review the situation and offer support?
answer: A time-safe next-assessment forecast found a useful but limited signal: at the reviewed threshold, about 62% of alerts were correct and 42% of actual assessment problems were found, with a median 26 days before the due date.
conclusion: Earlier assessment history carried the clearest predictive information, while recent participation added timing and context. The result may support a carefully governed human review process, but it does not justify an automatic decision about a student.

data.source: Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 349
data.population: 32,593 anonymized student-course attempts across 22 course presentations
data.analyticalUnit: One weekly snapshot for one student-course attempt with an upcoming non-exam assessment and known due date

keyFacts.population: eligible weekly snapshots in the later 2014J test period
2014J snapshots whose next assessment was missing by its due date or scored below 40

weekly snapshots flagged at the reviewed 0.50 threshold

target.definition: next assessment is missing by its due day or receives a score below 40
target.exclusions: Exams are excluded because their due dates are often unavailable in OULAD.

modelExplanation.outcome: Whether the next non-exam assessment with a known due date would be missing by that date or receive a score below 40
modelExplanation.predictionTime: At the end of each course week, before the next eligible assessment was due
modelExplanation.observation: One weekly snapshot for one student in one course attempt
modelExplanation.featureTypes: Recent and cumulative platform activity, prior submissions and scores known by that week, already-missing assessments, progress, and course context; demographic fields were not used

families.name: Prevalence baseline
families.plainLanguage: It gave every weekly snapshot the same event rate seen in the training courses.
families.reason: It set the minimum no-personalization reference.

families.name: SQL rule baseline
families.plainLanguage: It used fixed checks for inactivity, earlier missing work, or declining engagement.
families.reason: It provided a transparent rule-based comparison.

families.name: Regularized logistic regression
families.plainLanguage: It combined the available measures into an additive score while shrinking unstable coefficients.
families.reason: It provided an inspectable statistical reference.

families.name: Constrained decision tree
families.plainLanguage: It used a short sequence of if-then splits.
families.reason: It tested a simple nonlinear alternative that a person could still inspect.

families.name: Gradient-boosted decision trees
families.plainLanguage: They built many shallow trees in sequence so later trees could correct earlier errors.
families.reason: They tested whether interactions and nonlinear patterns improved ranking.

families.name: Calibrated logistic regression
families.plainLanguage: It adjusted the logistic regression probabilities using the 2014B validation courses.
families.reason: It provided an inspectable probability and workload reference for the alert example.

modelExplanation.strongestRanking: Gradient-boosted decision trees ranked the later 2014J cases best, with precision-recall AUC 0.642.
modelExplanation.bestProbabilities: Gradient-boosted decision trees also had the lowest later-test Brier score, 0.123; lower probability error is better.
modelExplanation.thresholdExample: The worked 0.50 cutoff used calibrated logistic regression: it flagged 14.4% of 117,186 later-test weekly snapshots, with 61.6% precision, 42.1% recall, and a median 26-day lead for correct alerts.
modelExplanation.retainedReference: Calibrated logistic regression remains the recommended inspectable reference, not the top-scoring model.
modelExplanation.selectionCriterion: I valued coefficients, preprocessing, probability adjustment, and cutoff behavior that another analyst could inspect. Predictive performance mattered, but it was not the only criterion because the score would affect human review workload and potentially sensitive outreach.
modelExplanation.practicalUse: The result demonstrates retrospective prioritization on later historical courses. It has not been prospectively validated or used in an operational support process.
modelExplanation.prohibitedUses: The output should never automatically grade, admit, discipline, rank, surveil, or deny an opportunity to a student, and it should never be treated as a measure of intelligence, motivation, effort, or need.

limitation: Platform clicks do not measure learning or motivation, historical associations do not explain why a student struggled, and the forecast has not been prospectively validated for operational use.
